{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "He crossed the rest of the way without counting planks. At the far posts the woman did not step back to make room, so he stopped on the last board with the stone between them, the photograph held out over it like something being passed across a counter.

He took it. It was warm from her hand, or from the turning. The face was small and grey and looking off toward an edge the camera had not kept. A child, he thought, or someone standing the way children stand, weight on one foot, already leaving.

"You know him," she said. It was not a question, and it was not quite a statement either. It was the kind of thing one says to hear whether it sounds true.

"I don't know," Tomas said. "I might."

She nodded as if that were the answer she had come for. Behind her the path went up through wet grass to a line of trees, and beyond the trees there was nothing he could see, only the grey the photograph was made of.

He looked back. The boy stood at the two stone posts on the other side, hands in his pockets, exactly where Tomas had left him, and for a moment the river made the distance seem wrong, as if the bridge had lengthened while he wasn't watching.

"Bring it back when you're sure," the woman said, and she turned and started up the grass without waiting to see whether he followed or stayed.

He stayed. The bridge hummed once under him, the low chord, and was quiet."}
